cards.claim: An algebraic equation is an equality involving variables and contains an equality sign.
cards.quote: An algebraic equation is an equality involving variables . It has an equality sign

cards.claim: In an equation the LHS and RHS have equal values only for certain values of the variable; those values are the solutions of the equation.
cards.quote: In an equation the values of the expressions on the LHS and RHS are equal . This happens to be true only for certain values of the variable. These values are the solutions of the equation.

cards.claim: Equations formed from linear expressions in one variable are called linear equations in one variable.
cards.quote: Here we will deal with equations with linear expressions in one variable only. Such equations are known as linear equations in one variable.

cards.claim: An equation, unlike an identity, need not be true for all values of its variables; only an identity holds for every value.
cards.quote: An algebraic identity is an equation that is true for all values of the variables occurring in it, while an equation need not be true for all values.

cards.claim: After solving y + 9 = 16 to get y = 7, the solution is checked by substituting it back into the original equation: 7 + 9 = 16 is true.
cards.quote: You can check that y = 7 is the correct solution by substituting it back into the original equation.

cards.claim: A learner may claim a wrong value (x = 40) solves (1/2)x = 80; the source presents this belief as wrong and asks why.
cards.quote: Emiliano thinks x = 40 x = 40 is the solution to the equation 1 2 x = 80 1 2 x = 80 . Explain why he is wrong.
